subject: Feature flag vendor: contract options & migration timeline
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
To: aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com, marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com, laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com
Cc: procurement@vendorservices.co
Date: 2026-10-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Feature flag vendor — contract window coming up (Q4)

Hi team,

Our LaunchDarkly contract has a full-term renewal window in mid-November. I want to start a quick cross-functional review: pricing, engineering impact, and whether we should continue with LD, try Optimizely (proof of concept), or consider a partial migration to open-source/backoff. Short ask: can procurement kick off updated quotes and two vendors (LD + Optimizely) plus a 6-week migration impact assessment?

What's useful to surface:
- Current spend and committed seats (Marcus, can you drop numbers?)
- Any outstanding feature gaps we rely on (Aditya)
- Timeline constraints from product roadmaps (Laura)

I attached the basic ask doc and the migration-risk template for prefill. Ideally procurement gets vendor responses by 10/9 so we can review and pick a path before renewal notices.

Thanks — Hannah

[attachment: FF_migration_Risk_log.md (markdown)]
From: Sara Meyers <sara@launchdarkly.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>, marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2026-10-06T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Feature flag vendor — updated pricing and migration notes

Hi Hannah / Marcus,

Thanks for the heads-up. Attached is our updated Q4 pricing and an outline of account-level discounts we can extend based on commit levels. High level: we can hold current pricing through the end of Q1 if you sign a 12-month renewal by Nov 20. We also included a migration playbook (lift & optimize) for large customers moving services across environments — usually a 4–6 week program for critical flags.

Key notes:
- Enterprise streaming and relay configuration: no downtime expected for standard migrations.
- SRE involvement: recommended 1 engineer for cutover + 1 for validation.
- Data retention / audit logs: configurable, export available for legal/retention audits.

Attachments: LD_pricing_Q4_2026.pdf

Happy to jump on a 30-min call next week to walk through the discounts.

Best,
Sara Meyers
Enterprise Accounts — LaunchDarkly
[sara@launchdarkly.com]
From: Theo Park <theo@optimizely.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@vendorservices.co
Date: 2026-10-07T08:47:00-07:00
Subject: Optimizely proposal for feature management (summary)

Hi Hannah,

We heard you're evaluating options — attaching a concise proposal and a sample migration timeline. Optimizely can offer a bundled discount if you consolidate experimentation and feature gating under one contract; typical engagements include a migration sprint and a 30-day validation window. The attached spreadsheet has line-item pricing and professional services hours.

Notable differences versus LD: Live experiment rollbacks are identical in function; Optimizely charges per seat+events at scale which can look different on our billing side. We included a sample cost model for your traffic profile.

Attachments: Opti_proposal_2026.xlsx

If useful, I can set up an architecture review with our onboarding team next Tuesday.

Regards,
Theo Park
Solutions Engineering — Optimizely
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com, laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2026-10-09T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Feature flag vendor — contract options & migration timeline

Quick technical readout after scanning both proposals and a short sync with infra:

Pros/cons (high level):
- LaunchDarkly: proven at scale, streaming infra already in our infra pattern; lower migration risk; pricing more predictable if we accept a committed seat model.
- Optimizely: attractive if we want a single experimentation + gating product; migration risk slightly higher due to event/SDK differences (we'll need a small adapter layer for rollout orchestration).

Estimated engineering effort for a full migration: 4–6 weeks (sprint-aligned) for feature flag parity + 2 weeks for validation and cleanup. That's assuming 1-2 engineers + 0.5 SRE. If we do a hybrid approach (keep LD for core infra, try Optimizely on new products) we can reduce risk and spread cost.

Attachments: I filled the FF_migration_Risk_log.md with baseline risks and estimated dev hours.

Thoughts: I'm leaning toward renewing LD for the core infra and piloting Optimizely for experimentation on two new product teams. That gives us time to evaluate costs and avoids a big cutover during Q4.

– Aditya
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com>
To: aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com, marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com, laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Sara Meyers <sara@launchdarkly.com>, Theo Park <theo@optimizely.com>, procurement@vendorservices.co
Date: 2026-10-12T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Feature flag vendor — decision & next steps

Team — thanks for the fast turn. Summary & next steps: 

1) Path: We will pursue a 12-month renewal with LaunchDarkly for core feature gating (commit to existing footprint, sign by Nov 18) and run a 3–month Optimizely pilot for experimentation on two non-critical product teams.
2) Procurement: Please work with Sara on the renewal quote and a documented SLA addendum; Marcus, confirm final seat counts and commit level by EOD 10/14.
3) Engineering: Aditya, please produce a 2-week pilot runbook (objectives, success criteria, rollback plan) for Optimizely by 10/16. Allocate one engineer + 0.5 SRE.
4) Commercial: Hannah will negotiate a good-faith transition clause in the LD contract for up to 30 days of migration support if/until we expand Optimizely.

Sara/Theo — appreciate the rapid response. We'll loop back to schedule the architecture walkthroughs once procurement has final numbers.

Thanks — Hannah
Director, Platform Product — Redwood Inference
[hannah.schmitt@redwoodinference.com]
